A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SG-KBQA work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable, and relocated or renamed material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original GrailQA and WebQSP experiments, component ablations, parameter studies, runtime measurements, and error analyses.

after.justification: V3 retains original experimental results and adds CWQ evaluation, Hit scores, retrieval measurements, and fallback-use statistics.

M1.justification: The retrieval, sketch parsing, candidate pruning, deferred disambiguation, schema-conditioned generation, and fallback procedures remain substantively unchanged. SER groups the earlier RG-EMD/RG-CER components, while SLFG names the existing generation module; these are organizational changes rather than new algorithms.

E1.justification: V3 adds ComplexWebQuestions (CWQ), containing 34,689 questions requiring up to four-hop reasoning. This substantially expands evaluation of complex I.I.D. questions beyond WebQSP. GrailQA and WebQSP coverage is retained.

E2.justification: The WebQSP comparison in Table 2 adds RoG, ToG, ICSU, and FiDeLiS, while removing TIARA and FC-KBQA from that comparison. This broadens comparison to reasoning and agentic methods. The GrailQA leaderboard comparator set remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Existing GrailQA/WebQSP splits and core training settings remain unchanged. V3 adds CWQ's 80/10/10 split and 20-epoch generator training, Hit evaluation, and reproduced ToG F1 results using GPT-4-turbo. The main retrieval ablation now replaces SER with TIARA linking results instead of separately removing mention-detection and candidate-retrieval components.

E4.justification: V3 adds entity-retrieval F1 and relation-recall analyses in Appendix J, fallback-use rates in Figure 4, and a WebQSP fallback ablation. It replaces or extends the qualitative cases, replaces separate RG-EMD/RG-CER ablations with a SER ablation, and removes the DeepSeek backbone test. The GrailQA fallback ablation and parameter sweeps already existed in v1.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests. The sampled error analysis does not introduce uncertainty estimation and remains unchanged.

E6.justification: The headline GrailQA and WebQSP scores remain unchanged. V3 adds CWQ F1 of 78.2, overall entity-retrieval F1 of 90.5, Hit comparisons, fallback rates, and revised ablation results; DeepSeek results are removed. Table 3 corrects compositional F1 from 84.6 to 83.6, matching v1's appendix. New WebQSP Hit results place SG-KBQA at 84.1 versus FiDeLiS at 84.3.

T1.justification: The KB and ontology definitions, S-expression operator semantics, and Equations 1–3 remain substantively unchanged. Expanded or relocated examples introduce no new mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion expand the performance claim from two benchmarks to three, incorporating CWQ. The central schema-guided generalization contributions and claimed GrailQA leaderboard improvements remain unchanged.

C2.justification: V3 adds interpretations of larger EM gains, limited fallback reliance, and tolerance of noisy relation candidates. It replaces the categorical statement that fine-tuning is required with an explanation based on insufficient demonstration diversity, and removes the DeepSeek-specific explanation. The main schema-connectivity rationale and existing training-data and retrieval limitations remain.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces a promised code release with stated availability and an explicit repository address. Appendix D clarifies dataset-specific training and split use, and the main text supplies CWQ's training budget. Most hyperparameters, hardware information, and runtime measurements are retained.

R1.justification: Related work substantially expands to LLM reasoning trajectories and agentic KBQA, including RoG, GCR, ToG, ICSU, and FiDeLiS. V3 more explicitly distinguishes its sketches from sketch-filling approaches such as RetinaQA and acknowledges untested parallel work READS and MemQ. The DeepSeek discussion and citation are removed.

P1.justification: The introduction and related work are extensively rewritten around schema-first processing and the SER/SLFG terminology. Method subsections are repartitioned, WebQSP details move into the main setup, and detailed ablation and applicability material is consolidated from appendices into the main discussion.

P2.justification: Introductory and pipeline diagrams are redrawn, and the ontology illustration is reworked in Appendix A. The prompt screenshot becomes a formatted table. Main ablation and applicability tables incorporate appendix EM results, while new Hit/retrieval tables, fallback and recall plots, and a redesigned case-study figure substantially revise the presentation.

improvement.justification: V3 strengthens the generalization explanation with direct retrieval measurements, broader CWQ and recent-baseline comparisons, clearer diagrams, and code-access information. These gains are tempered by less granular component ablations and new numerical inconsistencies: Section 5.3 reports a 0.9-point fallback F1 drop, whereas Table 3 shows 88.5 versus 84.6, a 3.9-point drop. Overall, the evidence and exposition improve, but important reporting weaknesses remain.
